newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm, traders see rise.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm, traders see rise.

text.p: Leading Russian shares firmed in early trade on Thursday and dealers said the market could close slightly higher despite fluctuations throughout the day.
"We can expect the market to rise by the end of the day," said, Ivan Deryabin, a trader at MFK-Moscow Partners.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 shares opened at 349.91 after closing on Wednesday at 349.75.

National electricity utility UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.3089 at GMT 1005 from $0.2999 at Wednesday's close. Regional power company Mosenergo MSNG.RTS edged up to $1.359 from $1.350 while oil producer Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS firmed to $0.878 from $0.875.
"We're observing a fairly tenacious demand, active Western clients and average volumes," said Aton trader Alexander Bobolev.
But Creditanstalt-Grant trader Andrei Galperin said the morning rise should be seen in the context of what he called the temporary flucuations of the past few days.

"I think the first-tier market is going to be bobbing up and down now since investors have turned their interest to the second tier," Galperin said, adding that the market would continue to fluctuate until June.

Traders said investors were showing special interest in regional "energo" electricity utilities on the RTS-2 market for less liquid shares, and head of Rinaco Plus's corporate securities department Andrei Kukk said car factories would also be hits this summer.
"They have very few shares on the market and small capitalisation.
